question: A shopkeeper lists the price of a fan at 60% above its cost price and offers a 15% discount on its list price. If he earns a profit of ₹117, then what is the list price (in ₹) of the fan?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup % × Discount % ÷ 100)

Net Profit % = 60 − 15 − (60 × 15 ÷ 100) = 45 − 9 = 36%

36% of CP = Profit = ₹117

⇒ CP = 117 × 100 ÷ 36 = ₹325

⇒ List Price = 160% of CP = 325 × 1.6 = ₹520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 60%

Discount Percentage = 15%

Profit = ₹117

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit = SP − Cost Price (CP)

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP = 100x
 
 SP = 136x
 
 MP = 160x
 

 Markup = +60%
 

 Profit = ₹117
 

 Discount = -15%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the fan be 100x.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100x + 60% of 100x = 160x

⇒ Discount = 15% of 160x = 24x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 160x − 24x = 136x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 136x − 100x = 36x

⇒ We are given the actual profit is ₹117.

⇒ 36x = 117

⇒ x = 117 ÷ 36 = 3.25

⇒ List Price (MP) = 160x = 160 × 3.25 = ₹520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Profit/Loss Percentage

When a markup and discount are given, Net Profit % = M − D − (M × D) ÷ 100, where M is Markup % and D is Discount %.

Marked Price (List Price)

It is the price listed or printed on an article. A shopkeeper calculates discounts exclusively on the Marked Price, while Profit or Loss is derived from the Cost Price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, Effective Discount = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.
